title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #1
body: Ask the score. Not the university, the ball. Everyone in this country remembers their number out of 700 the way other people remember a birthday, and they will tell you within four minutes unprompted. Above 650 gets mentioned immediately. Below 500 gets mentioned never. It's a sealed deal if he can still name the exact question he got wrong in the exam four years ago.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #2
body: Ask whether it's state-funded or paid, because that single word restructures the entire conversation. Dövlət hesabına is a quiet flex delivered flatly. Ödənişli is delivered faster, with a joke attached, to get ahead of it. Both of them know exactly what the other one is. It's a sealed deal if a parent has ever said the tuition figure out loud in front of guests.
caption:
Tip #2 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #3
body: Find out if he's from Baku or from a rayon. This is the real divide and nobody discusses it directly. The Baku student goes home for lunch. The rayon student lives in a yataqxana or shares a flat with three others, sends money home, goes back at Novruz with a bag, and works harder than everyone. It's a sealed deal if he says the name of his town and then immediately explains where it is, before anyone asks.
caption:
Tip #3 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #4
body: Ask about attendance. Davamiyyət is a currency and everyone is running a deficit. There is a person in every group who signs in for four people. There is a professor everyone is afraid of and a professor whose lectures nobody has attended since October. It's a sealed deal if he can tell you his exact attendance percentage per subject, from memory, and it's the only number he tracks.
caption:
Tip #4 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #5
body: Watch where he eats. Yeməkxana if broke, the shawarma place outside if slightly less broke, and one café where a coffee lasts three hours and counts as studying. He is not studying. Nobody at that table is studying. It's a sealed deal if the group has a specific table and someone gets genuinely annoyed when it's taken.
caption:
Tip #5 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #6
body: Ask about Erasmus. Everyone applied. Everyone has a friend who went to Poland or Portugal and came back different. The application is a whole season, the motivation letter got rewritten nine times, and half the year is waiting for an email. If he went, he mentions it constantly. If he didn't, he mentions that he almost did. It's a sealed deal if he still has the rejection saved.
caption:
Tip #6 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a Baku University Student. Tip #7
body: Ask what happens after graduation, and watch it get vague fast. Military service, a master's abroad, or a junior role at a bank, and most people are holding all three options open because committing to one means admitting the other two are gone. He will say "görək" and change the subject. It's a sealed deal if his mother has a clearer plan for his life than he does and she has told you about it.
caption:
Tip #7 😭 ADA, BHOS, UNEC, BDU, you're all in here.
